Synopsis:
Steeps Evacuation: a family tries to get smuggled past the absolute ships and out of the city. They don't have enough cash so dad decides to stay and let mum and the kids leave first. This is the smuggler, Captain Sleam.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_SteepsEvacuation_Sailor.json: Dharin and Leepak Brislen are a family trying to be smuggled past the Absolute ships out of the city toward Waterdeep; they lack funds to buy passage for everyone, so Dharin has insisted Leepak and their daughters go first while he stays behind. Captain Sleam is the smuggler hired to run them out — he expects full payment and fears his crew will punish him if he takes unpaid “freeloaders.” Off-screen, this is a tense, emotional farewell under immediate threat from the Absolutes: Dharin is anxious, relieved, and deeply grateful for the sacrifice, while Leepak alternates between fury at the smuggler’s perceived greed and relief that her children might get out. The player’s lines in the excerpts represent an outside intervention (negotiation or coercion) pushing Sleam to accept the father aboard despite the lack of funds; Sleam’s responses reflect his practical worry about crew repercussions and his willingness to be persuaded.
- LOW_SteepsEvacuation_Mother.json: Leepak Brislen is the mother in a family scrambling to be smuggled past the Absolute ships out of the city toward Waterdeep. The Brislens can't afford passage for all four of them, so Dharin — the girls' father — has insisted Leepak and the daughters go first while he stays behind. Her lines are aimed at the smuggler or helper arranging their escape: she alternates between fury at the smuggler's perceived greed and deep relief and gratitude that her family can leave. This is a tense, emotional farewell under the immediate threat of the Absolutes, with the family's safety hinging on the smuggler's cooperation.
- LOW_SteepsEvacuation_Father.json: Dharin Brislen is a desperate father arranging for his family to be smuggled past the Absolute ships and out of the city to Waterdeep. He and his partner Leepak (the girls’ mother) lack the funds to buy passage for everyone, so Dharin has insisted that Leepak and their daughters go first while he stays behind. The lines are directed at the smuggler or helper facilitating their escape — he’s anxious, relieved, and deeply grateful for the sacrifice being made on his family’s behalf. This is a tense, emotional farewell with the city’s occupying forces (the Absolutes) posing an immediate threat.
- WYR_MerchantsHouse_RefugeeLeader.json: General dialog for the refugee leader - father of the refugee family who stayed in the merchant's house when he was away.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_BereavedFather.json: A father that recently lost his child and has come to the graveyard with his wife to get a specially made coffin. In one set, the coffin maker has refused to make it as he's too busy - father is very upset. In the other set he's extremely thankful to the player for organising the coffin for his daughter.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Captain Sleam: This is life and death for me too, mate. You only get as many berths on my sloop as you can pay for. If I allow any freeloaders, my own crew will scrag me. (node 1)
- Player: Captain... Sleam, is it? It would be a shame to split up the family, don't you think? Let the father go with them. (node 0)
- : True (node 9)
- Captain Sleam: Very well, I'll do it. I suppose I can find some way to make it good with the crew. (node 8)

Sample 2:
- Captain Sleam: This is life and death for me too, mate. You only get as many berths on my sloop as you can pay for. If I allow any freeloaders, my own crew will scrag me. (node 1)
- Player: I have news for you, Captain: you're going to accept four for the price of three and take the father aboard. Or I'll pitch you into the harbour. Got it? (node 12)
- : True (node 11)
- Captain Sleam: That's, er, a very convincing proposal, saer. I'll do just as you say. (node 2)

context: Dharin and Leepak Brislen and their two daughters are trying to be smuggled past the Absolute ships to Waterdeep but lack funds for everyone, so Dharin has insisted that Leepak and the girls go first while he stays behind. Captain Sleam is the smuggler hired to run them out; he expects full payment and fears his crew will punish him if he carries unpaid “freeloaders.” Off‑screen this is a tense, emotional farewell under immediate threat from the Absolutes — Dharin is anxious and grateful, Leepak alternates fury and relief — and the family’s safety hinges on Sleam’s cooperation. The player in the excerpts is an outside intervenor who pressures or coerces Sleam to accept the unpaid father aboard; Sleam initially resists for practical reasons but can be persuaded.
